samples.question: A 5 by 5 grid of square cells stands on a white card, with a column of five large coloured tags on the left, one beside every row.  An amber tag marks a 'two' row; a violet tag marks a 'three' row.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the grid a key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole grid by this rule: for every cell, count how many of its eight surrounding neighbours (the cells that touch it along an edge or at a corner) are dark.  A cell on an amber row becomes dark in the next round if and only if that count is exactly two; a cell on a violet row becomes dark if and only if that count is exactly three; in every other case the cell becomes pale.  Note that a dark cell may turn pale and a pale cell may turn dark.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting grid of the next round, and keep the row tags fixed.  After the last round, count how many cells in the 5 by 5 grid are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.
